Subject: Ground support for Zephyr onsite — arrivals spread across day

Hi Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks again for coordinating logistics for our customer workshop on June 9. Our attendees are arriving on staggered flights between 08:30 and 15:00. Key asks:

- We want a reliable car-service option for 6 execs traveling from SFO (individual transfers, meet-and-greet at baggage claim).
- A secondary rideshare fallback for smaller groups (2–3 pax) if car service is delayed.
- Parking passes for two rental cars (on-site overnight).
- A driver escort for the final VIP convoy leaving at 17:00 on day 2 (to the airport).

Can you share recommended vendors, estimated costs, and an operational failover plan if flights are delayed? Also, any curb-access rules at the venue we should be aware of.

Appreciate it — Alyssa
Alyssa Greene
Event Lead, Zephyr Systems
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ground support for Zephyr onsite — arrivals spread across day

Alyssa —

Thanks — putting operational plan below. High-level options (cost/latency tradeoffs) and contingencies: 

1) Dedicated car service (preferred for execs)
   - Vendor: Summit Car & Shuttle (economy, exec sedans, 2 x 6-pass vans for entourage)
   - Pros: consistent ETA, meet-and-greet, luggage handling, driver scripts for VIP handling
   - Cons: higher OPEX; requires load-zone reservation for curb access

2) Hybrid rideshare + meet-point plan (fallback for groups of 2–3)
   - Pre-book ride credits with preferred provider, establish a single meet point (Garage A, Door 3) to avoid curb queuing
   - Use prefix codes in our calendar invites to tag arrivals for CS ops to trigger pop-up help (see driver_script_v3.txt)

3) Short-term rentals (rental cars)
   - Use 2 rental vehicles on a single corporate card; we will pre-authorize and submit plates for venue parking passes

Contingencies / failovers: 
- Flight delay > 45 minutes: switch from car-service pick to rideshare for non-VIP travelers; Summit will hold a 30-minute courtesy wait for confirmed VIPs (policy in ratecard).
- Severe congestion (curb blocked): park at Loading Lot B (10 min shuttle) and deploy a short coach shuttle for 8+ pax.
- Driver no-show: escalate to Summit ops (ops@summitshuttle.com) and trigger on-call backup driver (Ben to own).

Action items: 
- Ben: confirm Summit rates and a 2-hour courtesy window; attach contract link when available.
- Lauren: confirm plates for rentals and request two overnight parking passes from venue.
- Marissa (me): finalize driver script and passenger manifest; circulate final rundown by Thursday.

I attached the current driver script and the venue curb map for your review. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk the flows.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Program Manager, Events — Redwood Inference

Quick operational notes from venue ops contact (Chris Murray copied below):

- Curb access: single-lane load zone in front of Entrance 2; 5 min loading max per vehicle unless a pre-authorized load permit is issued.
- Loading Lot B can be reserved for 30–90 minute windows for shuttle staging; requires a site liaison during deployment (Chris suggested the on-site Zephyr lead or our event manager).
- There is a dedicated short-term staging area for ridehail drop-offs 200m from main entrance (we should map a covered walk and signage).

Costs: preliminary quote from Summit attached (economy sedan $65, exec sedan $95, 6-pass van $170/hr). They will hold cars at the airport for 30 min free for VIPs.

Ben
